raw_response: {"diagnosis":"Batch 14 was re-delivered at 05:00 with 338 rows duplicating txn_ids already delivered at 02:00. The re-delivered copies have txn_ts as epoch milliseconds, which breaks the TIMESTAMP cast. The epoch value 1768716261000 equals 2026-01-18 06:04:21 UTC, the same instant as the original copy. The fix parses both timestamp formats and keeps one row per txn_id, which also stops the duplicates from inflating counts and sums.","decision":"fix","confidence":0.9,"pre_sql":[],"step_overrides":{"silver_transactions":"CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE silver_transactions AS SELECT CAST(txn_id AS BIGINT) AS txn_id, customer_id, CAST(merchant_id AS INTEGER) AS merchant_id, CAST(amount AS DECIMAL(12,2)) AS amount, CASE WHEN regexp_matches(txn_ts, '^[0-9]+$') THEN epoch_ms(CAST(txn_ts AS BIGINT)) ELSE CAST(txn_ts AS TIMESTAMP) END AS txn_ts, CAST(CASE WHEN regexp_matches(txn_ts, '^[0-9]+$') THEN epoch_ms(CAST(txn_ts AS BIGINT)) ELSE CAST(txn_ts AS TIMESTAMP) END AS DATE) AS txn_date FROM raw_transactions WHERE status = 'POSTED' QUALIFY row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY txn_id ORDER BY ingest_ts ASC, batch_id ASC) = 1;"}}
